Day, K.S.Mudagal J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Challenging the award dated 21.06.2019 passed in MVC No.5416/2016, the Insurer has preferred MFA No.7208/2019 and claimant No.1 has preferred MFA No.6777/2021.
2.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Deceased Lakshmi was employed in Lanco Company engaged in constructing the road near Bheemakkanahalli village, Hosakote-Chintamani road falling within the jurisdiction of Nandagudi Police Station.
On 03.08.2014 at 11.00 a.m. when Lakshmi was working, in the process of taking motor grader No.KA 07 M 2494 reverse side that hit Lakshmi.
She suffered grievous injuries and was shifted to Srishti Hospital situated at H.Cross.
On giving preliminary treatment she was shifted to K.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, at 2.00 p.m. she was declared dead.

4. The claimants initially filed MVC No.181/2015 before the Principal District and Sessions Judge,
Kolar claiming that they are the husband and mother of deceased Lakshmi and they are entitled for compensation from the respondents for her accidental death.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: When that matter was pending, on 27.08.2016 they filed another petition in MVC No.5416/2016 before the III Addl. Small Causes Judge and MACT (SCCH-18), Bengaluru against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-.

entities.text: III Addl. Small Causes Judge and MACT (SCCH-18), Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By that time in MVC No.181/2015 the first claimant had even led his evidence.
Subsequently on 23.06.2017 the claimants filed memo in MVC No.181/2015 for withdrawal of the said petition.
Ultimately on 08.07.2017 that petition was dismissed as withdrawn.
5. In MVC No.5416/2016 the claimants contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of motor grader by its driver.
They further claimed that they were dependent on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, respondents are liable to pay the compensation.

3 6.
At the relevant time, respondents No.1 and 2 were the owner and insurer of Road Grader No.KA-07 M 2494.

Respondent No.1 alone contested the petition denying the occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving of the motor grader, age, occupation, income of the deceased and its liability to pay the compensation.

7. The Tribunal on recording the evidence and hearing the parties by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Road Grader No. KA 07 M 2494 and that the claimants are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased.

8. The Tribunal relying on the post-mortem report considered the age of the deceased as 25 years,
notionally considered her income at Rs.6,500/- per month, added 40% to the same by way of future prospects, deducted one-third from her income for her personal expenses, applied multiplier of 18 and awarded compensation of Rs.13,10,500/- on the head of loss of dependency.

9. The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.14,20,500/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 13,10,500/-
 2. Loss of consortium 80,000/-
 4. Loss of Estate 15,000/-
 5. Transportation of dead body, 15,000/-
funeral
expenses & obsequies

Ceremony expenses  Total 14,20,500/-
Submissions of Smt. Geetharaj, learned counsel for the Insurer:
10. The claimants' own documents more particularly the inquest report show that the deceased was unmarried.
The other documents produced by the claimants for proof of the relationship with the deceased were all subsequent to the filing of the petition.
Apparently they were got up documents.
When the claimants came before the Court, the initial burden of proving relationship was on them.
The Tribunal committed error in holding them to be the husband and mother of the deceased based on the alleged admission of respondent No.1 in the pleadings.
The said admission was not unambiguous, clear and unequivocal.
The claimants filing two petitions, withdrawing them and pleading ignorance about the earlier petition show their sinister motive of making wrongful gains.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

Submissions of learned counsel for the claimants:
11. So far as the relationship, the first respondent in its written statement admitted the same.
Therefore, it cannot resile from the same.
Apart from that there are innumerable documents in proof of the relationship of the claimants with the deceased.

The entries in Ex.P6 inquest report and Devaraj @ Devappa vs The Manager on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101819317/
4 Ex.P7 PM report were not at the instance of the claimants.

entities.text: Devaraj @ Devappa vs The Manager on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, they will not become conclusive proof.
The order of the Tribunal with regard to relationship does not warrant interference of this Court.
The compensation awarded on the head of loss of dependency is on the lower side.
Analysis 12.
The parties are not at dispute, regarding occurrence of the accident and the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Road Grader by its driver.

The questions for consideration are:
1. Whether the claimants proved the relationship with the deceased ?
2. Whether the compensation awarded is just one?
Reg. claimants' relationship with the deceased:
13. Claimant Nos.1 and 2 in the petition claimed that they are the husband and mother of the deceased respectively.

Claimant No.1 claimed to be from Madakal village of Sedam Taluk,
Kalaburagi District.

Claimant No.2 claims to be the resident of Ingalagi Village, Chittapur Taluk,
Kalaburagi District.
The accident as already pointed out took place within the limits of Nandagudi Police Station, Hoskote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.
When the claimants claim that they are the husband and mother of the deceased, the initial burden of proving the same is on them.

14. In para No.3 of the statement of objections answering the claim of relationship of the claimants,
respondent No.1 stated as follows:
"It is submitted that petitioner No.1 is the husband of the deceased only the legal dependent of the deceased.
The petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased is not the legal dependent on the earnings of the deceased.
The petitioner should strictly prove that she is only the legal heir and they were not dependents on the earnings of the deceased."
15. It is settled law
that to call a statement as admission, the same should be clear and unequivocal.
But the above extracted paragraph goes to show that language of para No.3 of the written statement was incoherent.
Ultimately respondent No.1 called upon the claimants to prove that they were the legal representatives/ dependents of the deceased.

Therefore that cannot be called as an admission within the meaning of Section 17 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
16.
The complaint was filed by Venkappa S/o Bheemaiah.
In the complaint Ex.P1, it is stated that he was residing with his wife Ananthamma, sons Devaraju, Shamarao, Nagesh and his granddaughter Lakshmi.
In the entire complaint, there is no whisper about Lakshmi being married.
Under the circumstances, the claimants had to discharge their initial burden of proving that they were the husband and mother of the deceased.

Devaraj @ Devappa vs The Manager on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101819317/
5 17.
In column No.6 of Ex.P6 Inquest report, claimants' own document it is stated that the deceased was unmarried.

Even in column No.9 of the alleged statement of the grandmother of the deceased,
there is no whisper about Lakshmi being married to claimant No.1.
Having produced and - 10 - relied on Ex.P6, the claimants cannot demand that Court shall only rely on part of the said document and reject the other part.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs. Premlata Shukla and others1 has held that once a document is produced and proved in evidence, the party producing such document cannot later resile from the other part.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs. Premlata Shukla and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no merit in the contention that the statement in Ex.P6 that the deceased was unmarried shall be ignored.
However in column No.10 the statement of one Sharanappa is to the effect that deceased Lakshmi was grand daughter of Venkatappa and claimant No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
18. According to the claimants, claimant No.1 was married to the deceased one month prior to the accident.
Except the self serving statement of PWs.1 and 2 which was disputed, absolutely there was no material in proof of the marriage of claimant No.1 with the deceased.
He did not even produce any documents like Ration Card or Voters Card to show that she lived with him in his house as his wife.
Apart from that the claimants filed multiple petitions on the same ground.
Claimant No.1 tendered the evidence in other case.
(2007) 13 SCC 476 - 11 - While giving evidence in the present case he denies that he had deposed in the earlier case.
Such conduct of claimant No.1 also creates doubt about the credibility of his evidence.

Under the aforesaid circumstance, the Tribunal was not justified in holding that claimant No.1 was the husband of the deceased solely based on the alleged admission of respondent No.1 in its written statement.
So far as claimant No.2 the finding of the Tribunal that she is the mother of the deceased is sustainable in view of the evidence discussed above.

Reg. Quantum of Compensation:
19.
Though the claimants contended that the deceased was earning Rs.9,000/- per month, there was no proof of actual income.
In their earlier petition, they had claimed that she was earning Rs.6,500/- per month.
The accident took place in the year 2014.
The deceased was working in Road Construction.
The prevailing the rate of wages during that period was not less than Rs.8,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal was not justified in considering her income at Rs.6,500/- per month.
20 . As per the P.M report, she was 25 years employed in private establishment.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble - 12 - Devaraj @ Devappa vs The Manager on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101819317/
6
Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi2

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 40% of her income has to be superadded by way of future prospects, which comes to Rs.11,900/- (8,500+3,400).
Since it is held that the deceased was unmarried, half of such income has to be deducted for her living expenses.
Therefore the income to be computed on the head of loss of dependency comes to Rs.11,900/2=5,950/-.
The applicable multiplier is 18.

Therefore the compensation payable on the head of loss of dependency comes to Rs.12,85,200/- (5950X12X18).
21.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case the second claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.44,000/- on the head of loss of consortium.
She is entitled to compensation of Rs.30,000/- on the heads of loss of estate and funeral expenses with an escalation of 10%.

The just compensation payable to claimant No.2 is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 12,85,200/-

2 . Loss of consortium 44,000/-
 4. Loss of Estate 16,500/-
 AIR 2017 SC 5157  - 13 -  5. Transportation of dead body, 16,500/-
 funeral expenses & obsequies  Ceremony expenses  Total 13,62,200/-
 22.
Grant of interest is no doubt a matter of discretion, but that should be based on reasoning.
The Tribunal has not assigned any reason for granting interest at 9% per annum.
Having regard to Section 34 of CPC, it would be just and proper to award interest at 6% per annum.
Considering the delay in filing the appeal by the claimants, this Court by the order dated 10.03.2022 denied interest for the delayed period of 189 days.
The first respondent-Insurer is entitled to that benefit in calculating the interest.
23. For the aforesaid reasons, both the appeals deserve to be allowed in part.
The impugned award needs to be modified accordingly.

Hence the following:

 c) Respondent No.1-Insurer shall deposit the  said amount, on adjusting the amount already deposited if any, within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
d) On such deposit, the Tribunal shall release 50% of the amount to claimant No.2 on she duly furnishing required documents.
e) The balance 50% shall be invested in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of three years.
 f) MFA No.6777/2021 is disposed of  accordingly.
 g) Registry shall transmit the amount in  deposit if any and TCRs to the Tribunal  forthwith.
